title: Backup agents
summary: Hired teams that support mages in a crisis.

claims.text: Backup agents bring covering fire, extraction, getaways, or quieter help such as moving gear, passing messages, clean-up and paperwork.
They serve a group and are loyal to it, but most of all they work for pay, so in a hopeless fight they pull back or run.
Teams have a leader who calls the moves, so they do not take orders from the mage they guard.

title: Avatars as characters
summary: The inner gods of mages given a face.

claims.text: A mage may perceive an Avatar as anything from a whisper to a seemingly separate person.
Most Avatars have no body and so no Physical Traits, except those made real through the Manifest Avatar Merit.
Great spirits such as Papa Legba are principles wearing a shape, here transition and passage, and deserve respect beyond their outward look.

title: La Huesera, the Bone Woman
summary: A spirit who gathers the bones of the forgotten.

claims.text: Bone Woman collects remains of vanishing animals such as wolves and polar bears, and of people nobody stops to remember.
Bone Woman draws no line between beasts and humans, seeing all as different peoples.
La Huesera has never been known to bring back anyone's loved one, holding that those who are mourned already live on in memory.
Bone Woman rebuilds the dead over weeks or months with beads, wire, wood and scraps, singing in the local native tongues.

title: Lady Aelida, the Lady of Feathers
summary: A riddling spirit who wears the face of someone trusted.

claims.text: Aelida takes the form of whoever the viewer trusts most, but always wears a feather somewhere on that guise.
Aelida's feathers hold Tass, about five points each, and are sometimes given to mages who lend aid.
Aelida speaks in riddles and opposes the Technocracy and anyone who would bind the world to one form.

title: Bygones
summary: Mythic beasts that the modern world no longer believes in.

claims.text: Griffins, imps, unicorns and their like suffer Unbelief Paradox outside the Umbrae and need a steady feed of Quintessence from human keepers.
Thrown into public view, often by Marauders, they tend to die within minutes and their bodies rot or fade soon after.
Small Bygones can serve as Chantry guards, or blend into local belief if they keep their true nature quiet.
